sentences.text: Due to matrimonial differences between petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2, the parties started residing separately from 14.02.2021.

Subsequently, respondent no.2/complainant registered an FIR against the petitioner no. 1 (husband), petitioner no. 2 (mother-in-law), petitioner no. 3 (brother-in-law) and petitioner no. 4 (sister-in-law).
6. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the parties have arrived at settlement before the Mediation Centre, Saket Courts, Delhi, vide Settlement Agreement dated 26.11.2024, .
It is further stated that the parties are living together, at their matrimonial home, since 29.12.2024, alongwith their minor son.

7. The present petition was listed before the learned Joint Registrar on 02.05.2025, wherein statement of respondent no. 2 has been recorded as under:-
"1.
I am the Respondent no. 2 in the present petition.

At my instance, FIR bearing no.
387/2023, Under Section 498-A/406/34 was registered at PS Jaitpur, Delhi against the petitioner.
The charge sheet has been filed against the petitioners.
2. The matrimonial dispute between me and all the petitioners have been amicably settled as per mediation settlement deed dated 26.11.2024.

The mediation settlement has been arrived at between myself and petitioners without any force, coercion,
undue influence and pressure.
I have signed the mediation settlement deed with my wish and will.

The settlement is on record as Annexure P-3 at page 75.
3.

Pursuant to the mediation settlement deed dated 26.11.2024, I am happily residing with the petitioner no. 1 (Sh. Vineet Kumar) in my matrimonial home peacefully after reconciling all the issues and disputes.

4. I do not wish to pursue the present FIR bearing no. 387/2023, Under Section 498-A/406/34 registered at PS Jaitpur, Delhi therefore, the same be quashed along with all proceedings emanating therefrom.
I have no objection if the said FIR is quashed.
I shall abide by all the terms of the settlement.

My affidavit of No objection is at page 29-30.
5.
I shall be bound by my statement as stated above."

The parties have undertaken to abide by their reciprocal obligations as agreed in the aforesaid settlement agreement.
10. In view of the settlement between the parties, learned APP for the State also has no objection if the present FIR is quashed.

11. In Gian Singh v. State of Punjab (2012) 10 SCC 303, Hon'ble Supreme Court has recognized the need of amicable resolution of disputes by observing as under:-
"61.

entities.text: Gian Singh v. State of Punjab (2012) 10 SCC 303
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In other words, the High Court must consider whether it would be unfair or contrary to the interest of justice to continue with the criminal proceedings or continuation of criminal proceedings would tantamount to abuse of process of law despite settlement and compromise between the victim and the wrongdoer and whether to secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that criminal case is put to an end and if the answer to the above question(s) is in the affirmative, the High Court shall be well within its jurisdiction to quash the criminal proceedings."
12.

In view of the aforesaid circumstances, and the fact that the parties have put a quietus to the dispute, no useful purpose will be served in continuing with the present FIR No. 387/2023, under Sections 498A/406/34 of the IPC, registered at P.S. Jaitpur and all other consequential proceedings emanating therefrom, including the chargesheet pending before the Court of Ms. Archita Garg,
learned Metropolitan Magistrate, (South- East), Saket Courts, Delhi.

In the interest of justice, the petition is allowed, and the FIR No. 387/2023, under Sections 498A/406/34 of the IPC, registered at P.S. Jaitpur and all other consequential proceedings emanating therefrom, including the chargesheet pending before the Court of Ms. Archita Garg,
learned Metropolitan Magistrate, (South-East), Saket Courts, Delhi,
is hereby quashed.
14. Petition is allowed and disposed of accordingly.
15. Pending application(s), if any, also stand disposed of.
